definition: Unconventional therapy refers to alternative forms of treatment that are used outside usual medical care. In this source, the term points to unproven treatments that people may rely on instead of evidence-based approaches.

reasons: The packet supports only that ‘unconventional therapy’ refers to unproven alternative treatments; it does not support the broader claim that these are simply treatments used outside usual medical care.
The statement that people may rely on these ‘instead of evidence-based approaches’ is not stated in the packet and adds an unsupported contrast.
The packet does not support the claim that unconventional therapy is used “outside usual medical care.”

The packet supports that it is “unproven alternative treatments” (via the need to limit reliance on unproven alternative treatments), but it does not support that the term “points to unproven treatments” in general beyond this dengue context.
The packet does not support the additional framing that people rely on it “instead of evidence-based approaches.”

The definition makes substantive generalizations about the term that are not explicitly stated in the provided text (it is only referenced in relation to dengue fever and public reliance on unproven alternatives).
